text: In December 2019 we converged first on a bill. One hundred twenty of us said "costs now act," one hundred nineteen said "drug costs now act," one hundred seventeen said "lower drug costs now act," all peaking on the twelfth. Debbie Dingell said it first, in September. Ninety-seven of us reached for "cummings lower drug costs now act" and ninety-four for "the elijah e," both introduced by Nancy Pelosi in October, the day the measure took a name. Eighty-eight of us said "prescription drug costs," eighty-five "of prescription drugs." Then, on the eighteenth, one hundred ten of us said "articles of impeachment" — a phrase first recorded, the record notes, by Susan M. Collins, not one of us. Two peaks, six days apart: the drug bill, then the impeachment. We said the same words on the same days. The record shows we moved together.

top_phrases.phrase: cummings lower drug costs now act
